messages:
Aisha: :rotating_light: Lyra Health (lyra-prod vpc) - seeing sustained 503s from dedicated pool serving lyra-frontend. Errors spiked ~ 11:07 UTC, traffic partially degraded, customers in EU affected. paging on-call now. thread created for mitigation and customer comm planning.
IncidentBot: [automated] Pager triggered: lyra-prod_vpc_high_5xx at 1769504321. On-call: @aisha, escalation to @jon if not ack in 5m. Links: https://ops.redwood/alerts/lyra-1769504321
Aisha: acked. Gonna gather quick status. Anyone near the dedicated pool metrics?
Raj: I can pull metrics. Looking at grafana - error rate 5xx went from 0.2% to 12% around 11:07 UTC. P95 latency also jumped from 120ms -> 450ms. CPU on pool-gpu-3 jumped, memory stable. Here's the query I ran:
```
sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"redwood-serving\",customer=\"lyra\",code=~\"5..\"}[5m])) by (instance)
```
Priya: joining bridge. Oncall switchover in 10m if needed. I have runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood/tenant-isolation
Jon: I'm next-level oncall. If this is tenant isolation/eviction we need to confirm whether it's noisy neighbor or model load. Check KV cache size and ongoing heavy prompts.
Emily: I see a pattern of large context requests from a small subset of lyra-sessions (session IDs in the query). Possibly a query storm from a scheduled job in their infra. I can grep logs. Running:
```
rg \"session_id\" -g 'logs/lyra/*.log' | cut -d' ' -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head
```
Raj: logs confirm ~600 requests from session x9a3 in a 2m window, all long-context completions (~8k tokens). This is flooding the dedicated pool's concurrency slots.
Aisha: mitigation options: 1) throttle requests from offending sessions (reverse-proxy), 2) temporarily scale up lyra dedicated pool if capacity available, 3) failover to a smaller compatible model in hosted fallback. Preference to avoid broad customer traffic impact.
Priya: executing throttling rule on edge for those session IDs now. Pushing config:
```
POST /edge/config
{
  \"route\": \"lyra-prod/*\",
  \"throttle\": {
    \"match\": {\"session_id\": [\"x9a3\"]},
    \"rate\": \"5/s\"
  }
}
```
Priya: throttle applied. Edge reports 95% drop in that session's traffic to the pool. Observed 5xx rate dropping.
Jon: good. Also activating warm standby model (lyra-standby-v1) in regional warm pool to absorb traffic spikes. Running rollout:
```
redwood serve promote --customer lyra --model lyra-standby-v1 --pool warm-eu-1
```
IncidentBot: [automated] Route change detected and warm pool promotion initiated by @jon at 1769505120.
Raj: metrics now: 5xx down to 1.1% in last 3m, p95 latency trending down to 180ms. CPU on pool-gpu-3 decreasing.
Aisha: happy path: incident mitigated by throttling + warm pool. Next: customer comm and credits proposal. @maria-cs can you draft the customer note? We need a brief, timeline, mitigation steps, and proposed credit per SLA.
Maria-CS: on it. Draft below 2
0 please edit for technical accuracy and tone. Meant for Lyra's Ops and Execs.

```
Hi Lyra team,

Thank you for your patience  we observed a service degradation impacting API requests routed to your dedicated pool between 11:07:38 UTC on 2026-03-14. We identified a concentrated request storm from a small subset of sessions that caused resource contention and elevated error rates. Immediate steps taken:

- Throttled offending sessions at the edge to stop the storm (11:12 UTC)
- Promoted standby model into regional warm pool to absorb residual traffic (11:15 UTC)
- Monitored and verified recovery; error rates returned to baseline by 11:38 UTC

Impact: Partial request failures and increased latency for some EU customers during the window. No customer data was exposed. We are preparing an RCA and a timeline of preventive actions.

Proposed remediation and follow-ups:
- Implement session-level rate-limiting for long-context requests (complete by 2026-03-20)
- Add automated detection of anomalous session-based request storms (complete by 2026-03-27)
- Provide credit for SLA breach as calculated below (TBD)

We99ll share a formal RCA within 3 business days and remain available for a live briefing.

Regards,
Maria, Redwood CS
```
Jon: technical note for the RCA  include: root cause (unthrottled long-context job on customer side), why isolation failed to fully protect capacity (concurrency exhaustion on dedicated pool due to model KV cache warmup and large left-shift token windows), and mitigations (edge throttles, warm pool promotion, suggested quota protection).
Emily: add logs/queries + correlation with queue depth and KV hit-rate. I can attach sample logs (redact PII).
Tomo-Finance: on credits  per their Dedicated SLA, 99.9% monthly uptime; for the 31-minute window, estimated credit calc:
- Monthly seconds: 2,592,000
- Outage seconds: 1,860
- SLA credit tier suggests pro-rated credit = (outage / month) * reserved fee * SLA factor. Rough immediate estimate: $1,250 credit. Will finalize after accurate usage slice.
Aisha: ok agree tentatively. We'll confirm exact amount and include in customer comm once final.
Priya: creating internal RCA draft doc and assigning owners. Link: https://docs.redwood/rca/lyra-1769504321
Priya: initial root cause summary in doc: \"customer-side job produced sustained high-concurrency long-context requests causing resource contention in dedicated pool; edge lacked per-session hard caps.\" Will expand timeline and remediation.
Maria-CS: small tone note for customer comm: avoid technical jargon around KV caches; propose 'heavy request pattern from a small number of sessions' instead. Keep it brief and action-oriented.
Jon: agree. For exec brief, propose 3 bullets: severity, customer impact, proposed credits + timeline to close mitigations. I'll draft high-level for VP Eng.

Jon: EXECS DRAFT:
```
At ~11:07 UTC Lyra experienced partial degradation due to a high-rate long-context request storm from a subset of sessions hitting their dedicated inference pool. Mitigation: edge throttling and warm-standby promotion restored service by 11:38 UTC. Proposed customer credit ~$1.2k and technical mitigations scheduled. RCA to be delivered in 3 business days.
```
Maria-CS: sending draft to Lyra after we confirm credit amount and remove technical noise. I'll propose a 30-min briefing window if they want.
Aisha: owners and timeline check:
- Customer comm draft: Maria (send after finance confirm)  by EOD today
- Final credit amount: Tomo  by EOD today
- RCA doc: Priya + Emily + Jon  initial draft in 48h, final in 3 business days
- Action items for infra: implement per-session request cap + anomaly detection  infra team (Jon/Emily)  POC by 2026-03-20
Priya: tagging follow-ups in ops board. Creating a retrospective card and linking to RCA doc.
Maria-CS: prepared an incision-free customer note, will send after Tomo confirms. Suggest optional live call 2pm UTC.
Tomo-Finance: confirmed final credit will be $1,275. I'll add write-up and ledger entry, cc billing. 
Aisha: will notify Lyra execs with Jon's 3-bullet exec summary + Maria's customer-friendly note. Any objections? :thumbsup:
Jon: :thumbsup: ready for exec send.
Emily: :thumbsup: attaching redacted sample logs to RCA doc.
Priya: closing live bridge. Leaving channel open for follow-ups and customer reply. Thanks team.
IncidentBot: [automated] Bridge closed by @priya at 1769509621. Duration: 55m. Incident state: mitigated.
Aisha: Filing post-incident follow-ups: scheduled RCA delivery 2026-03-17 16:00 UTC, customer email queued for 2026-03-15 18:00 UTC pending Tomo final. Tagging @maria-cs for send and @jon for exec note. Good work all. :heart:
